programme: FOS and JUND form the AP-1 immediate-early dimer; XBP1 is the transcriptional arm of the same IRE1-driven unfolded-protein response whose kinase arm (via TRAF2-ASK1-JNK) converges on FOS/JUN family proteins. Together they mark an inducible stress-and-proliferation switch downstream of receptor/ER-stress signaling, not a constitutive lineage programme.
role_in_a: In papillary RCC, HGF-MET signaling (the driver pathway of type 1 papillary RCC) induces immediate-early c-fos as part of tubular mitogenic response, and FH-deficient tumors on the type 2/HLRCC end of the papillary spectrum show IRE1-XBP1 UPR activation as a metabolic adaptation to asparagine/nutrient stress.
role_in_b: Expected rather than documented here: AP-1 activation and IRE1-XBP1 UPR signaling are broadly recognized stress-adaptation and invasion pathways in glial tumors, but nothing in the retrieved record places FOS, JUND, or XBP1 specifically in lower-grade glioma. The one glioma-specific hit in this factor set (NR5A2, chemosensitization via miR-433-3p) sits outside this programme.
shared_axis: Both tumor types arise in tissues where the driving lesion (MET-activated growth signaling in papillary RCC; hypoxic/metabolic stress in glioma) can route through receptor-triggered AP-1 induction and ER-stress-triggered XBP1 splicing as a shared, tissue-agnostic stress-response module, rather than through any kidney-brain-specific biology.
reasoning: The three-factor programme is a real, specifically nameable complex/pathway relationship (AP-1 dimer plus its UPR-linked XBP1 partner), so this is not incoherent. But only the kidney side has any placing literature, that literature is tangential (renal tubular mitogenesis, not papillary RCC by name; FH-deficient RCC, not confirmed as this exact cohort), nothing places any of the three factors in LGG, and kidney and brain are not an anatomically or clinically obvious pairing — so the connection rests on general stress-pathway reasoning rather than retrieved evidence.
support: PMID 9652757 — FOS induced downstream of HGF-stimulated renal tubular mitogenesis, the growth pathway (HGF/MET) that drives papillary RCC. PMID 32774853 — XBP1/UPR activation in fumarate-hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma, the FH-deficient end of the papillary RCC morphologic spectrum. No PMID above places FOS, JUND, or XBP1 in lower-grade glioma.
how_to_falsify: In an HGF/MET-driven papillary RCC line and an IDH-mutant lower-grade-glioma line, block the IRE1 RNase (e.g., 4μ8C) to stop XBP1 splicing and separately express dominant-negative FOS/JUN (TAM67) or knock down FOS/JUND; if the shared axis is real, both manipulations should measurably reduce AP-1/UPR target-gene induction and blunt proliferation or invasion in both lines under matched stress conditions. No change in either line's target genes or phenotype would falsify the account.
caveats: Kidney and brain share no obvious anatomy, embryology, or clinical overlap, so any shared axis has to be argued through a general cancer-stress mechanism rather than tissue logic. The 434 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the apparent replication is not as independent as the raw count suggests. Excluded single-view factors (PITX3, BCOR, HHEX, etc.) and tissue-generic factors (STAT4, RFX5, EGR4, HDAC7, FOXP3) are correctly absent from this account, not overlooked. ZBTB16 and ZBTB32 — known heterodimerizing BTB-zinc-finger paralogs — recur at similar frequency to the named programme but returned zero literature in either disease, so no account could be built for them without inferring novelty from silence; they are left out rather than forced in. NR5A2, despite the highest recurrence (178/434) and the only disease-specific hit on the glioma side, does not connect mechanistically to the AP-1/UPR programme and is treated here as a separate, unexplained signal.
